title: TDDR Rising Narratives — Saturday evening, Nov 21
summary: A snapshot of opposition narratives from the Right and the Far Left as of 5:20 PM ET Saturday, Nov 21, 2026. Built for TDDR (Too Dumb Didn't Read). Mayor Zohran Mamdani's Rikers closure plan is still the Right's biggest story at 23,849 posts in 24 hours, but daytime posts fell from 37,172 on Friday to 9,821 today, and the most-seen posts now include replies pointing out the plan pushes closure later, to 2032. The day's biggest mover on the Right was Stephen A. Smith's barbershop line, 'You secure that voting bloc, you don't need the Black vote.' Right influencers recast it as a Democratic plan to 'replace' Black voters (one post, 87,648 views), and the 'Democrats are importing voters' card jumped to 5,095 posts (4.38× its prior average). Noncitizens cannot vote in federal elections. At 3:14 PM ET President Trump posted a chart titled 'Democrats Hurt Stocks' ('-8.7%, ~$5.9 Trillion'), and the market-blame query reached 10,317 posts (6.24×). The math is right; the cause is oversimplified, and the new Congress isn't sworn in until January. New on the Far Left: after Trump reposted Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed's gold 'TrumpCare' card, Medicare for All posts hit 1,697 in the 4 PM hour (12,571 in 24 hours), and the left's message to Democratic leaders is 'out of excuses.' The 'nullify the midterms' call script bounced back in daytime hours (4,257 posts). Three faded cards were dropped. Every count, quote and fact-check comes from sources and X queries pulled this evening or carried over from this morning and labeled. Nothing here is invented.

The only political trend was 'Cornyn' (19,238). X News ties it to outgoing Sen. John Cornyn's blue-slip hold on a Trump judicial nominee in Texas and his opposition to Rep. Wesley Hunt's nomination as ambassador to Saudi Arabia, an intra-Republican fight we did not score as an opposition narrative. 'Rikers' and 'Mamdani,' which earned the Rikers card this morning's trend bonus, were no longer on the list, so no card received the trend bonus this evening. Several trend objects had no tweet_count ('Mateer,' 'Arthur Smith,' 'GMac,' 'Ty Benefield,' 'Rich Rod,' 'Heupel,' 'Jelani McDonald,' 'Grant Wilson,' 'TTUN,' 'Anthony Colandrea,' 'Chase Sowell,' 'Austin Mack,' 'Panamá Centro'); their volumes are unavailable and we did not estimate them.

oppositionNote.body: Right = narratives the Right is pushing after the Democratic midterm wave. Far Left = pressure on Democratic leadership and the incoming majority from the party's left. The Rikers card is a Right attack on a Democratic mayor; we include it because Mamdani is being used as the national face of the party. The market card is tagged Right because the 'Democrats crashed the market' frame comes from the Right, even though many posts matching the query are rebuttals. The immigration card is tagged Right because the 'replacing Black voters' frame is the Right's reading of Stephen A. Smith's comments; Smith is a Democratic voter. The new Medicare for All card is tagged Far Left because the pressure is on Jeffries, Schumer and the incoming majority to deliver it now, even though Trump amplified the pitch and many matching posts come from his base opposing it. The Iran-funding and Van Hollen cards are tagged Far Left because the pressure on Jeffries and Schumer comes from the party's left. The Social Security card stays tagged Right because the 'Ponzi scheme' frame is a Right talking point. The tag is the primary opposition frame.

methodology: Last updated Saturday, Nov 21, 2026, 5:20 PM ET. This is a research snapshot for TDDR, not a live API, and it will go stale. U.S. X trends were pulled at about 5:07 PM ET. This morning's snapshot (Nov 21, 7:20 AM ET) is kept in the archive and was not overwritten. Nine of its twelve narratives were re-counted with the same queries so momentum compares like with like. The new 24-hour window overlaps this morning's by 14 hours (5 PM Friday to 7 AM Saturday ET), so we also report each query's 7 AM–5 PM ET daytime count against the same hours on Friday. Three narratives were dropped because they faded: the Erie noncitizen-voting card (458 posts in the last 24 hours, 0.73× its prior daily average; 296 from 7 AM to 5 PM ET versus 950 the same hours Friday); the 'Democrats are coming for your paycheck' tax-hike card (698 posts, 0.52×; 283 versus 1,146); and the 'blue wave was rigged' card (1,769 posts, 0.28×; 767 versus 1,668), whose claims now mostly travel inside the 'nullify the midterms' card. One was added with a new query: Medicare for All and 'TrumpCare.' Other candidates were counted and not carved out as cards: Minnesota welfare-fraud memes aimed at Gov. Tim Walz and Rep. Ilhan Omar (4,506 posts, 0.90×; 1,743 from 7 AM to 5 PM versus 3,120 on Friday); Jeffries and AIPAC after his New York Times interview (1,470 posts, 0.21×, folded into the Iran card); Jeffries's warning that 'MAGA extremists' should expect House investigations (529 posts, 0.73×); Sen. Tim Kaine's call to stop saying 'illegals' (141 posts, 11.75× a tiny baseline); and Mamdani's DSA donation video (25 posts on a donation-specific query).

For each narrative we ran one English-language X search with x.get_posts_counts_recent at hourly granularity over a 166-hour window from 7:00 PM ET Saturday, Nov 14, through 5:00 PM ET Saturday, Nov 21 (the 'seven-day' total; the API's recent-search limit is seven days back from the pull). The last 24 hourly buckets (5:00 PM ET Friday, Nov 20, through 5:00 PM ET Saturday, Nov 21) give the 24-hour count, and the hourly buckets were summed into UTC days for the daily charts. We counted named news or fact-check outlets whose coverage we opened or retrieved and cite on the card. Official government pages, bill text, advocacy groups, research groups, blogs, X News summaries, archives and X posts are cited as sources but not counted as outlets; Candid Dragon and FactCheck.org are cited on the market card but not added to its count. This evening we re-researched the market, immigration, Iran-funding and new Medicare for All cards; the other cards carry this morning's outlet counts and say so. We noted whether each topic appeared on the U.S. trends list at about 5:07 PM ET.

Score = 50% volume index + 30% acceleration index + 20% coverage index. Volume index is 100 × log10(1 + last-24h posts) / log10(1 + the highest last-24h count in this set). Acceleration index is 100 × min(last-24h / prior daily average, 3) / 3, so a triple-or-higher average scores 100. Prior daily average is (seven-day total − last 24h) / 6. Coverage index is 70 × min(outlets, 7) / 7, plus 30 if the topic was on the U.S. X trends list this evening. No card got the trend bonus this evening, which is the main reason the Rikers score fell. The Medicare for All query already carried about 9,000 to 18,000 posts a day all week, so its acceleration is modest even though its 4 PM hour was its busiest. The Van Hollen, popular-vote compact and Jeffries queries carry last week's spikes in their seven-day totals, which keeps their acceleration low. Read the post counts alongside the scores. Morning-to-evening score changes also reflect the lower volume ceiling (23,849 this evening versus 51,234 this morning) and how much coverage we retrieved.

Counts are query matches, not unique posts or unique users, and queries can overlap. The 'nullify' query overlaps the dropped rigged-midterms query. The market query requires a market term plus 'Democrats' or 'blue wave,' so it also catches rebuttals and general market posts that mention Democrats. The Rikers query also catches straight news posts and rebuttals. The Medicare for All query catches supporters, opponents and general health-care posts, and its 'M4A' term can catch unrelated uses. The Social Security query also catches posts attacking Johnson. The immigration query includes the phrase 'Stephen A,' so it can catch unrelated Stephen A. Smith posts; this evening most of its volume was about his immigration remarks. The impeachment query also catches Democrats discussing impeachment. Replies are included, and automated @grok replies make up a visible share of several queries. Sentiment is a qualitative label from relevancy-sorted post samples and from quotes in news coverage, not a scientific poll. This evening we pulled fresh samples for the Rikers, market, immigration, 'nullify' and Medicare for All queries. Other cards carry this morning's sentiment and say so. Daily bar charts use UTC days (a UTC day starts at 7:00 PM ET the previous evening). Bars marked * are partial windows. Hourly charts are labeled in ET.

disinfo.caveatBody: New this evening: Trump's 'Democrats Hurt Stocks' chart gets the numbers right and the cause wrong. The S&P 500 did fall 8.7% from the Nov. 3 close to the Nov. 20 close, and total U.S.-listed market value fell about $7.7 trillion (Candid Dragon's chatter check), but stocks rallied the day after the results, Friday's drop is tied mainly to the Nvidia accounting-probe report and the AI sell-off (Reuters; CNBC), and the new Congress is not sworn in until Jan. 3, 2027. 'Democrats are importing immigrants to replace Black voters' is Stephen A. Smith's stated belief, not an established fact: the census does count every resident for House seats, as the Constitution requires, but noncitizens cannot vote in federal elections (18 U.S.C. § 611), and PolitiFact has rated the related claim that millions of immigrants are registering to vote Pants on Fire. 'Trump endorsed Medicare for All' is overstated: he reposted El-Sayed's 'TrumpCare' card and praised Democrats' health-care ideas but has not backed a bill. Carried over from this morning: 'Mamdani is releasing thousands of criminals' and 'Mamdani is closing Rikers now' get the plan backward: it sets a target of no more than 4,100 people in custody by the end of 2032, reached through diversion and shorter case delays, keeps Rikers open until borough jails are built, and asks the City Council to move the legal deadline later, from August 2027 to 2032 (City of New York; City & State; Gothamist). The 'nullify the midterms' demand is still circulating as a phone script; the president has no authority to cancel state results or declare martial law (Brennan Center; Protect Democracy), and fact-checkers found no evidence that machines switched votes. 'The Protect Our Neighbors Act gives 1.6 million people green cards' is misleading; 'Democrats are already preparing a third impeachment' is a prediction by Jim Jordan, not a report; CNBC's experts say the 'Ponzi scheme' label misses how Social Security is funded, and PolitiFact has rated the comparison False when others made it; and 'Jeffries backs the Iran war' is false as stated.

narratives.sentiment: Angry and mocking on the Right ('JAIL BREAK IN NEW YORK'); fact-checking replies now make up much of the most-seen daytime sample
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Saturday, the top posts were smaller than overnight: @bluelivesmtr ('WTF is Mamdani doing,' 5,754 views), @LawEnforceToday ('clear Rikers Prison of almost half its inmates,' 563 views) and @ConstitustionX ('JAIL BREAK IN NEW YORK,' citing a cut of 'roughly 2,500 people — from about 6,600 down to 4,100,' 448 views). AllSides posted a right/left/center coverage comparison (692 views). Many of the remaining posts were replies pointing out that the 2019 City Council law already requires closure and that the plan moves the deadline later, to 2032 (@ReceiptsMatter, @StrayCatAgain). narratives.summary: Evening update (Nov 21): 23,849 posts in the last 24 hours, 3.59 times the prior daily average (this morning: 51,234 and 109.32×). From 7 AM to 5 PM ET Saturday the query matched 9,821 posts, versus 37,172 in the same hours Friday. Cooling in daytime hours. The most-seen daytime posts repeated the '2,500 fewer people in jail' figure as a 'jail break'; the plan's own target is no more than 4,100 people in custody by the end of 2032, down from about 6,600, through diversion and faster case processing (NYC Mayor's Office; Gothamist). We pulled a fresh post sample this evening; the outlet count is carried over from this morning. This morning's card (7:20 AM ET): Morning update (Nov 21): 51,234 posts in the last 24 hours, 109.32 times the prior daily average (last evening: 37,350 and 81.05×). From 5 PM ET Friday to 7 AM ET Saturday the query matched 14,039 posts, versus 98 in the same hours a night earlier. Rising overnight. Still the largest count in this snapshot by far, and 'Rikers' (62,598 posts) and 'Mamdani' (156,080) were both on the U.S. X trends list at about 7:05 AM ET. The most-viewed post overnight was @EricLDaugh quoting Rep. Brandon Gill (R-Texas): 'Democrats when they run for office: We just want to make your life more affordable. Democrats when they get power: Actually, we're defunding the police and closing the prisons' (101,116 views). New coverage this morning: the City Council plans a December oversight hearing and a bill from Council Member Sandy Nurse to move the legal deadline from August 2027 to the end of 2032 with benchmarks (City & State); Criminal Justice chair Selvena Brooks-Powers said 2027 'is not feasible' (City & State). The correction officers' union called the population cap 'ill-conceived' and 'irresponsible' (BBC). A visible counter-thread points out the plan actually keeps Rikers open about five years longer than current law.
talkingPoints: Mamdani is closing Rikers and letting thousands of criminals out.
You can't cut the jail population by 2,500 without releasing people charged with violent crimes.
First he cut the NYPD's protest unit, now he empties the jails.
This is what a Democratic socialist city looks like — and Democrats want it everywhere.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: Rep. Brandon Gill (R-Texas), @EricLDaugh (101,116 views), @WescottAmerica, @Helen4NY, New York Post opinion pages, and the Correction Officers' Benevolent Association. News coverage: AP, POLITICO, Gothamist, City & State and BBC. Supporters include Council Members Sandy Nurse and Tiffany Cabán and Council Speaker Julie Menin, who backs a 'responsible transition.'
narratives.whyItWorks: Crime and disorder are the Right's most reliable attack on big-city Democrats, and Mamdani is the most visible democratic socialist in office, so a jail story in New York becomes a national preview of 'Democratic rule.' Specific-sounding numbers (2,100, 2,500, 7,000) turn a six-year population target into an image of open cell doors. It also pairs with other Mamdani stories circulating Friday, such as his NYPD unit cut and his pitch for monthly DSA donations, to build a single picture.
narratives.audience: Outer-borough and suburban New Yorkers worried about crime, national conservative audiences who see Mamdani as the face of the Democratic left, and police and corrections-officer communities.
narratives.counter: Nobody is opening the doors on Friday. The plan sets a population target for the end of 2032, reached through diversion, supervised release and faster cases, and Rikers stays open until the borough jails are built (City of New York; Gothamist). Closing Rikers has been city law since 2019, passed under de Blasio; this plan actually pushes the deadline later, and it still needs City Council approval (AP). Take the real question seriously: critics doubt the target can be met safely, so answer with how many people are held on lower-level charges and how case delays will be cut, not with slogans.

narratives.title: 'Democrats Hurt Stocks' — Trump posts his own chart, and the market-blame frame climbs again into Saturday evening
narratives.query: (Nasdaq OR "stock market" OR "market crash" OR "Dow" OR "S&P 500" OR stocks) (Democrats OR Democrat OR Dems OR "blue wave") lang:en
narratives.sentiment: Gloating and alarmed ('DEMOCRATS CRASH THE STOCK MARKET… AGAIN!'); 401(k) fear, with a steady stream of 'they aren't in office yet' rebuttals
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Saturday, the frame spread through smaller accounts rather than one viral post: @Easthillz12 ('Wall Street is getting absolutely WRECKED,' 524 views), @JTitor17 ('President Trump says we've lost TRILLIONS in the market because Democrats won the midterms,' 461 views), @montoyalouis1 citing the '-8.7% and ~$5.9 trillion' chart (284 views) and @BEAR13328382 ('DEMOCRATS CRASH THE STOCK MARKET/ECONOMY… AGAIN!'). Replies blamed a Democratic congresswoman's 'rhetoric' for a '$5 trillion stock market crash.' Rebuttals cited the Nvidia accounting-probe report (@TotallyLogit) and fact-check-style reply threads. This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: Evening update (Nov 21): 10,317 posts in the last 24 hours, 6.24 times the prior daily average (this morning: 9,842 and 7.94×). From 7 AM to 5 PM ET Saturday the query matched 3,295 posts, versus 2,812 in the same hours Friday. Rising in daytime hours. New this evening: at 3:14 PM ET President Trump posted a chart titled 'Democrats Hurt Stocks' on Truth Social, showing the S&P 500 from Election Day to Nov. 20 with the caption 'Dropped -8.7% ~$5.9 Trillion Market Value Loss' (Trump's Truth archive). The query rose to 358 posts in the 3 PM hour and 477 in the 4 PM hour, its busiest daytime hours. The chart's 8.7% figure matches the S&P 500's close-to-close drop from Nov. 3 to Nov. 20, but it leaves out the 1.6% rally the day after the election and the Nvidia and AI-valuation sell-off reporters tie Friday's drop to (Candid Dragon's chatter check; CNBC; Reuters). We pulled a fresh post sample this evening; the outlet count is carried over from this morning. This morning's card (7:20 AM ET): New this morning. The query matched 9,842 posts in the last 24 hours (7.94× its prior daily average) and 17,279 over seven days; 7,027 came from 5 PM ET Friday to 7 AM ET Saturday, versus 3,170 in the same hours a night earlier, and the busiest hour was 7 PM Friday (1,026 posts). On Friday the Nasdaq fell 5.3%, erasing its 2026 gains, the S&P 500 fell 3.7% into a correction, and the Dow fell 1.9% (AP; NBC News). Reporting attributes the day mainly to an AI-stock sell-off: Nvidia fell 14% after Reuters reported an SEC probe of its accounting, Anthropic fell about 9% a day after its record IPO, and rising rates and slowing AI earnings growth weighed on stocks (CNBC; Reuters; Axios). The Right's frame is that Democrats crashed the market. Democrats' midterm wins are part of the story, since investors fear new limits on AI data centers (NBC News quotes one strategist calling the Nvidia crisis and the Democratic win 'a one-two punch'), but the incoming Congress is not sworn in until January 2027 and has passed nothing. The query also catches rebuttals and general market chatter that mentions Democrats, so read the count as attention, not agreement.
talkingPoints: Trump's chart says it all: Democrats hurt stocks, down 8.7% since Election Day.
Wall Street is getting destroyed by the Democrats.
Trump warned that a blue wave would crash the market, and he was right.
Your 401(k) just lost thousands because people voted for socialists.
Democrats promised affordability and delivered a $6 trillion loss.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: President Trump (a Truth Social chart titled 'Democrats Hurt Stocks,' posted 3:14 PM ET Saturday), @GuntherEagleman (119,550 views Friday), copy-paste accounts such as @SeanHannityStat and @NorthStarMIO, Bill Mitchell (per X News), Breitbart ('Markets Fear Democrat Communism'), and smaller reply accounts. X News summarized the 'blame game' and the corrections. News coverage of the sell-off: AP, Reuters, CNBC, NBC News and Axios.
narratives.whyItWorks: Markets are a scoreboard people check on their phones, and a red day right after an election invites a simple cause-and-effect story. Trump had predicted a crash if Democrats won, so the drop looks like a prophecy fulfilled to his base. There is a grain of truth to work with, because analysts do cite fear of Democratic limits on AI data centers, and retirement-account losses are personal and immediate. Few people will read past the headline to the Nvidia probe or the Anthropic IPO.
narratives.audience: Retirement savers and 401(k) holders, small investors who follow market influencers, Trump's base primed by his 'crash' prediction, and swing voters anxious about the economy.
narratives.counter: Democrats don't take power until January 3, 2027; Republicans still run Congress and the White House. Friday's drop was led by AI stocks: Nvidia fell 14% on an SEC accounting probe report and Anthropic fell after its record IPO (Reuters; CNBC). Fear of new data-center limits is one factor analysts name, so don't deny it; say it plainly, and point out the market also rallied the day after the election (The Crosscheck). Pivot to what voters asked for: lower costs, not a higher Nasdaq.

factChecks.claim: Democrats hurt stocks: the S&P 500 dropped 8.7%, about $5.9 trillion, since Election Day.
factChecks.rating: Numbers check out; the cause is oversimplified (TDDR read of Candid Dragon's data)
factChecks.detail: Candid Dragon's chatter check found the S&P 500 fell 8.70% from the Nov. 3 close (7,568.92) to the Nov. 20 close (6,910.39), and total U.S.-listed market value fell about $7.67 trillion, so the dollar figure is, if anything, understated. But stocks rallied the day after the results (S&P 500 +1.58%), Democrats' wins were one factor in the Nov. 5 drop through fears of AI data-center limits, and Friday's Nov. 20 drop is tied mainly to an SEC accounting-probe report on Nvidia and the AI sell-off. The new Congress is not sworn in until Jan. 3, 2027. FactCheck.org noted Trump also skipped the post-election rally when he blamed Democrats for an earlier drop.

factChecks.claim: Democrats caused the stock market crash.
factChecks.rating: Mixed (The Crosscheck, on the same claim about the Nov. 5 drop)
factChecks.detail: Reviewing the Nov. 5 sell-off, The Crosscheck rated the claim that the drop was 'based on the results of the Election' Mixed: reporting names Democrats' sweep as one driver through fears about AI data-center limits, but the market rallied 1.6% the day after the vote, the selling centered on AI stocks already sliding since October, and no newly elected Democrat had taken office. Friday's Nov. 20 drop was not separately rated; AP, Reuters and CNBC attribute it mainly to the Nvidia probe, the Anthropic IPO sell-off, rates and slowing AI earnings.

narratives.title: Stephen A. Smith: 'You secure that voting bloc, you don't need the Black vote' — the 'Democrats are importing voters' card more than quadruples its daytime count
narratives.query: ("Stephen A" OR "Protect Our Neighbors") (immigration OR immigrants OR "open borders" OR Democrats OR amnesty) lang:en
narratives.sentiment: Triumphant on the Right ('Stephen A. just said the quiet part out loud'); replacement framing aimed at Black voters, with some Black users pushing back
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Saturday, nearly every top post quoted Smith's barbershop clip: @bennyjohnson ('Stephen A. Smith just told Black Voters the TRUTH about Democrats' Plan to REPLACE them with ILLEGAL Alien Voters,' 5,890 likes, 1,651 reposts, 87,648 views), @EricLDaugh ('BOOM,' 76,687 views), @MarioNawfal ('The Democrats are now an anti-American party,' 37,246 views), @DefiantLs (17,506 views) and @GuntherEagleman (14,854 views). Smaller accounts added 'REPLACEMENT' and 'your 13% becomes optional.' Pushback was small but visible, such as a Black user replying that 'Stephen A. Smith doesn't speak for 40 million people.' This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: Evening update (Nov 21): 5,095 posts in the last 24 hours, 4.38 times the prior daily average (this morning: 2,016 and 1.88×). From 7 AM to 5 PM ET Saturday the query matched 3,980 posts, versus 872 in the same hours Friday. Rising in daytime hours. Stephen A. Smith's comments drove the jump. A Smith-focused query ("Stephen A" plus immigration, immigrants, "Black voters", census or Democrats) matched 4,677 of the last 24 hours' posts (4.18× its prior average), 3,800 of them between 7 AM and 5 PM ET. Smith, a lifelong Democratic voter, said at a Washington barbershop taping posted Nov. 18: 'I firmly believe immigration is about securing a voting bloc. You secure that voting bloc, you don't need the Black vote' (Yahoo Sports / The Comeback; ProfiloPolitics). Right influencers recast it Saturday morning as a Democratic plan to 'REPLACE' Black voters, and PJ Media wrote it up at 3:29 PM ET. Smith's census point is accurate (all residents are counted for House seats), but noncitizens cannot vote in federal elections, and Smith said he does not want law-abiding migrants deported. We pulled a fresh post sample and added PJ Media to the outlet count. This morning's card (7:20 AM ET): Morning update (Nov 21): 2,016 posts in the last 24 hours, 1.88 times the prior daily average (last evening: 2,649 and 2.78×). From 5 PM ET Friday to 7 AM ET Saturday the query matched 1,144 posts, versus 1,777 in the same hours a night earlier. Cooling overnight. The 'affordability became amnesty' frame kept spreading: @ImMeme0's post that Democrats 'promised Americans relief from crushing prices' but introduced the Protect Our Neighbors Act drew 12,812 views, and a former immigration-enforcement account posted a thread on the bill text. We did not re-research coverage for this card this morning, so its outlet count is carried over from last evening.
talkingPoints: Even Stephen A. says it: Democrats use immigration to secure a voting bloc so they don't need the Black vote.
The census counts illegal immigrants, so open borders buy blue states more House seats and electoral votes.
Democrats take Black voters for granted and are replacing them.
Democrats just filed amnesty: ignore a deportation order for 10 years and you get a green card.
They ran on affordability, and the first bill is for illegal immigrants.
narratives.amplifiers: Right: @bennyjohnson (87,648 views), @EricLDaugh (76,687), @MarioNawfal (37,246), @DefiantLs, @GuntherEagleman, @RealAmVoice, PJ Media, and former Border Patrol official Gregory Bovino ('Stephen A. is right… It's YOUR vote'). Origin: Stephen A. Smith's Nov. 18 'Straight Shooter' episode filmed at a Washington, D.C., barbershop. Pushback: commentator Roland Martin (per ProfiloPolitics). Bill thread carried over from this morning: @ElectionWiz, @RedWavePress, @Bubblebathgirl.
narratives.whyItWorks: A lifelong Democratic voter and one of the most famous Black media figures in the country gives the Right a messenger it cannot be accused of inventing, and the clip was filmed in a Black barbershop. It mixes a real grievance (Democrats taking Black loyalty for granted) and a real fact (the census counts all residents for House seats) with an unproven motive, so each step sounds reasonable. It lands three days after the Protect Our Neighbors Act gave the 'amnesty' frame a news peg.
narratives.audience: Black men who follow Smith and feel taken for granted by Democrats, immigration-restriction voters, sports-media audiences who don't follow politics closely, and Right influencers' X followings.
narratives.counter: Don't argue with Smith's frustration; agree that Democrats have to earn Black votes on prices, jobs and safety, which is what he actually asked for. Then separate the facts: noncitizens cannot vote in federal elections (18 U.S.C. § 611), and while the census does count every resident for apportionment, that rule is in the Constitution, not a Democratic plan. Smith himself says he doesn't want law-abiding, tax-paying migrants deported. On the bill: an order has to be 10 years old, the person needs 10 years of continuous presence and no serious conviction, and a judge can renew the order (bill text; ABC News).

factChecks.claim: The Protect Our Neighbors Act gives green cards to 1.6 million people with deportation orders.
factChecks.detail: The bill's sponsor puts the number of people with final removal orders at about 1.19 million; 1.6 million is an earlier ICE figure. The bill would let an order expire only after 10 years, allow a judge to renew it, and let a person petition for any status they are eligible for only after 10 years of continuous presence and no conviction for a crime punishable by more than a year. It does not hand out green cards automatically, and it has no path in the current Republican House. This is TDDR's read of the bill text and Simon's release, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: The Protect Our Neighbors Act would wipe out 1.6 million deportation orders.
factChecks.detail: About 1.6 million people have final removal orders (ICE testimony cited by ABC News), but the bill covers only orders at least 10 years old for people continuously present with no criminal conviction, and a judge could renew an order. No count of who would qualify has been published. This is TDDR's read of that reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: Democrats are bringing in immigrants so they can vote for Democrats.
factChecks.rating: Pants on Fire (PolitiFact, on a related claim)
factChecks.detail: PolitiFact rated Trump's claim that millions of immigrants are signing up to vote illegally Pants on Fire. Noncitizens, including green-card holders, cannot vote in federal elections under 18 U.S.C. § 611, and PolitiFact has found noncitizen voting rare. PolitiFact has not rated Smith's remarks or the new bill.

narratives.title: NEW: 'Even Trump wants it — pass Medicare for All' — Trump reposts El-Sayed's 'TrumpCare' card, and the left says leadership is out of excuses
narratives.query: ("Medicare for All" OR "M4A" OR TrumpCare) lang:en
narratives.sentiment: Giddy and pressuring on the left ('Leadership and 2028 hopefuls are officially out of excuses'); skeptical that Trump is sincere; angry rejection from parts of Trump's base
narratives.sentimentNote: In a relevancy sample of posts from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Saturday, the most-viewed post by far was @Popstonox: 'Donald Trump shares Abdul El-Sayed's Medicare For All proposal to Truth Social' (12,723 likes, 721 reposts, 372,266 views). @socialistadri clipped streamer Hasan Piker's reaction — 'he's most likely not sincere about this' but it 'might be a step forward' (24,287 views). Left posts turned it into a demand on Democrats: 'Leadership and 2028 hopefuls are officially out of excuses. Pass Medicare for All' (@UniqueHiFi) and 'if you pass POPULAR POLICIES like Medicare for All… there won't BE a future Republican majority' (@Tman2096). From the Right: 'Absolutely No Medicare For All. Nothing named TrumpCare' (@Jeni41671). This is a read of that sample, not a poll.
narratives.summary: New this evening. The query matched 12,571 posts in the last 24 hours (1.03× its prior daily average) and 85,926 over seven days, the second-largest count in this snapshot; 5,821 came from 7 AM to 5 PM ET Saturday, versus 4,727 in the same hours Friday, and the 4 PM hour Saturday was the busiest (1,697 posts). Medicare for All already drew steady traffic all week, so acceleration is modest; the jump came this afternoon. After saying on Fox News Saturday morning that Democrats 'have some good points on healthcare,' President Trump reposted on Truth Social Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed's (D-Mich.) Nov. 12 post offering him a gold 'TrumpCare' card: 'Donald, this is on the table. Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave' (The Washington Times; Mediaite; Daily Kos). On Friday Trump had said, 'We could end up with great healthcare in our country. We could end up better than dealing with the Republicans,' and Sen. Bernie Sanders said he looks 'forward to working' with him (Common Dreams). The Far Left frame is pressure on the incoming Democratic leadership: if Trump is open to it, Democrats have no excuse not to pass Medicare for All. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez said she is hopeful the new majority will pass a 'first phase' (X News). Trump has not endorsed a bill. The query also catches opposition and general health-care posts, so read the count as attention, not agreement.
talkingPoints: Even Trump says Democrats have good points on health care — pass Medicare for All.
Put his name on it if that's what it takes: TrumpCare for All.
Leadership and the 2028 hopefuls are out of excuses.
Deliver popular policies like Medicare for All, or the Republican majority comes back.
narratives.amplifiers: Left: Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed (@AbdulElSayed), Sen. Bernie Sanders, Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez ('first phase' push, per X News), streamer Hasan Piker (via @socialistadri, 24,287 views), Common Dreams and Daily Kos. Aggregators: @Popstonox (372,266 views). Trump himself amplified the pitch on Truth Social. Opposition from parts of Trump's base in replies.
narratives.whyItWorks: It is a rare moment when the left's signature demand seems to have the president's blessing, so it turns an old wish into a test of the new Democratic majority: if Trump is open, any delay looks like leadership's choice. The gold-card gag is funny, visual and easy to share, and the left gets to troll Trump and pressure Jeffries and Schumer in the same post. Broad public support for guaranteed coverage in polls gives it a majority-sounding frame.
narratives.audience: Progressive and DSA-aligned voters, Sanders and El-Sayed supporters, young voters who follow streamers like Hasan Piker, and health-cost-stressed independents; Trump's base is the hostile audience in replies.
narratives.counter: Take the opening seriously and make Trump own it: ask him to back specific steps Democrats can pass in the first 100 days, such as restoring the ACA tax credits and lowering drug prices, and then build toward broader coverage. Be honest that a repost is not a bill and that a full single-payer system needs 60 Senate votes or a rules change. The win for Democrats is a health-cost vote Trump can't veto without breaking his own word.

factChecks.detail: Trump reposted a screenshot of El-Sayed's post with the 'TrumpCare' card on Truth Social on Nov. 21 after saying Democrats 'have some good points on healthcare' and that a bipartisan deal could produce 'great healthcare' (The Washington Times; Mediaite). We found no statement from Trump backing a specific Medicare for All bill or single-payer design. This is TDDR's read of the reporting, not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

narratives.whyItWorks: 'Ponzi scheme' is a sticky, intuitive metaphor for a pay-as-you-go system, and genuine insolvency projections give it a factual hook. narratives.counter: Use his own walk-back: even Johnson now says he isn't proposing to shut it down. Then explain the difference: a Ponzi scheme is a fraud that hides how it works; Social Security is a public, legally mandated program that can be kept solvent by changing taxes or benefits (PolitiFact). factChecks.claim: Social Security adds to the national debt like a Ponzi scheme that will collapse.

factChecks.claim: Social Security is a Ponzi scheme.

It also noted the superficial similarity: current workers' taxes pay current retirees. PolitiFact has not rated Johnson's Nov. 18 remark.

narratives.amplifiers: Right: The Gateway Pundit (@gatewaypundit, 89,762 views on its post), @DavidJHarrisJr (16,632 views), @GailGolec, @jimhoft_, and many small accounts posting identical 'BREAKING' copy and the White House switchboard number. narratives.whyItWorks: It gives voters who cannot accept a blue wave a deadline (Jan. 3), a remedy (one presidential order) and a task (call the White House), which turns grievance into action. It comes from someone with real access: Ticktin says he knows Trump from their teens and has been in the Oval Office with Peters (MS NOW). narratives.audience: Hard-core 'stolen election' believers, Tina Peters supporters, Gateway Pundit and Telegram/Gab audiences, and older conservative voters primed by the 2020 fight.
narratives.counter: Say it plainly and calmly: the president has no power to cancel state election results, and no law lets him declare martial law (Brennan Center; Protect Democracy). On 'algorithms': Snopes, PolitiFact and FactCheck.org found no evidence that machines switched votes in the 2026 midterms; the reports traced to touchscreen errors that voters could correct. Point out that Republicans won races on the same machines. Don't amplify the phone-number campaign.

factChecks.claim: The president can nullify the 2026 midterm results and declare martial law.
factChecks.detail: The Constitution gives the president no power over how states run or certify elections, and no statute authorizes martial law. The Insurrection Act permits troop deployments to enforce the law, not to change results, and federal law bars armed federal officers at the polls. This row relies on legal analyses from the Brennan Center and Protect Democracy; it is not a rating from a fact-check outlet.

factChecks.claim: Voting machines switched votes in the 2026 midterms.
factChecks.detail: Snopes found no evidence machines switched votes in either direction during the 2026 midterms; the reports it reviewed likely reflected human error or touchscreen alignment problems, and voters can review selections before casting. PolitiFact and FactCheck.org reached similar conclusions in October. Ticktin's specific 'algorithm' claim was not separately rated.
